subject: Consolidated closure and verification playbook — June inference disruption
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@datastreamlabs.com>, Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@datastreamlabs.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-06-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Consolidated closure and verification playbook — June inference disruption

Hi Samira / Aaron,

Thanks again for your patience while we completed our internal investigation into the June 10th inference disruption that affected your production routes. Attached is a concise closure packet (redwood_consolidated_rca.pdf) and a short recovery playbook (recovery-playbook-v1.md) we will use with your team to verify fixes and guardrails.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Root cause: race condition in the KV-cache eviction logic that surfaced under a specific prefix-traffic pattern and large batch gen windows, causing evicted keys to be re-requested and triggering repeated cold-kernel fallbacks.
- Impact window: 2025-06-10T13:04:23Z — 2025-06-10T13:46:09Z (approx. 42 minutes).
- Customer-visible symptoms: increased token latency (2x–3x baseline), intermittent 503s for certain multi-turn chat routes.
- Immediate mitigations applied: emergency config change to reduce batching concurrency and enable the safe eviction guard (deployed 2025-06-10T13:58Z).

What’s in the packet:
- One-page RCA with timeline and evidence (redwood_consolidated_rca.pdf).
- Token/usage dump for your impacted routes (tokenization_token_metrics.csv).
- Recovery playbook with verification steps and acceptance checks (recovery-playbook-v1.md).

Requested next steps from you:
1) Please confirm two engineers who will act as verification leads for the sanity runs in the playbook.
2) Confirm whether you want the mitigation to remain in place for 72 hours or until you sign off on the verification steps.
3) If you’d like, we can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough (I can invite Marissa & Hannah) later today or tomorrow.

We recognize the disruption impacted your critical flows; we’re open to discussing credits and longer-term guardrails once you’ve validated the fixes.

Thanks,
David
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_consolidated_rca.pdf (pdf), recovery-playbook-v1.md (md), tokenization_token_metrics.csv (csv)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Samira Khan <samira.k@datastreamlabs.com>, Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@datastreamlabs.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-06-15T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Consolidated closure and verification playbook — technical mapping and integrity

Hi all — quick technical notes to answer the mapping / integrity questions.

Short answers up front: no user data exposure; the issue was confined to cache eviction/latency behavior. The spike maps to two production routes you run: /v1/chat/stream and /v1/generate/batch with a shared prefix used by your orchestration.

Detailed points:
- Root cause: an off-by-one condition in the eviction window calculation allowed a small subset of hot keys to be incorrectly flagged for eviction when concurrent large-batch requests reduced the effective concurrency window. This caused sudden cache misses and concurrent re-population attempts, which in turn triggered a software fallback path that took longer to initialize kernels for those sequences.
- Data integrity: cache misses may have increased recomputation but did not alter persisted state or logs — no PII exposure. We validated with our audit logs and HMAC checks.
- Mapping to CSV: rows 124–198 in tokenization_token_metrics.csv correspond to the impacted prefix (your account id: DSL-3742). I’ve attached a short mapping table as an inline snippet in the shared Drive folder.
- Immediate and permanent mitigations:
  * Deployed eviction-safety flag (temporary) to reduce false evictions — rolled at 2025-06-10T13:58Z.
  * Patch to the eviction window logic (PR #4821) queued with a staged rollout to canary on 2025-06-17 and full rollout pending sign-off.

Verification plan (Hannah will run with you):
1) Sanity traffic replay for impacted prefix at 0.5x, 1x, 2x baseline (check median and 95th percentile latency).
2) KV cache hit rate validation and re-check of HMAC audit logs.
3) Smoke tests for multi-turn chat flows.

I’ll join tomorrow’s walkthrough and bring the short mapping artifacts.

— Marissa
Senior Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference

Samira / Aaron — thanks for the walkthrough today. Quick summary and commitments so your audit trail has a single source of truth: 

Agreed verification items (owner / ETA):
- Hannah to run the verification playbook and share a short verification report (Hannah Schmitt) — due 2025-06-17T18:00:00Z.
- Marissa to merge & stage the eviction-window patch to canary (Marissa Cole) — staged 2025-06-17; full rollout pending verification.
- Sergio to provide a remediation credit proposal and formal language for procurement (Sergio Alvarez) — draft 2025-06-18.
- David to deliver the consolidated packet (this thread) to your procurement and execs, including a plain-language credit summary and the recorded walkthrough link.

Deliverables we attached/shared: redwood_consolidated_rca.pdf; recovery-playbook-v1.md; tokenization_token_metrics.csv; shared Drive mapping folder: https://drive.redwood.com/Shared/DSL-June10-RCA

Acceptance criteria for closure: verification report shows latencies within 10% of baseline 95th percentile and no recurring 503 signatures across replay windows. Once verified, we will schedule the Tier-1 rollback window for the staged patch and finalize the credit memo.

If you want a brief executive-ready text block for procurement, I can send a one-paragraph summary and the credit template today.

Appreciate the partnership — we’ll get this fully closed and produce the verification artifacts for your audit.

Best,
David Kim
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
